newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid Hussain profit helped by volume.
newsitem.headline: Rashid Hussain profit helped by volume.

text.p: Malaysia's leading institutional stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd said on Friday that its six-month rise in profit was helped by higher share volume traded on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
In a statement accompanying results for the half-year ended November 30, 1996, the company said pretax profit rose 17.7 percent to 203.9 million ringgit compared with a year ago.

The stronger profit was offset by general provisions made on customers' outstanding positions in accordance with its accounting policy and "a loss incurred by the futures subsidiary", Rashid Hussain said.
It did not disclose the size of the general provisions or the subsidiary's loss.
Income from associated companies rose by 4.2 percent, mainly due to higher contributions from DCB Holdings Bhd, which owns DCB Bank, the statement said.
The group's share of profit from the DCB Holdings group for the six months amounted to 47.9 million ringgit from 41.3 million ringgit in the previous period.

In November, Rashid Hussain announced a restructuring that included the acquisition of 75 percent of Kwong Yik Bank Bhd from Malayan Banking Bhd. The scheme is expected to be completed by June 1997, Rashid Hussain said.
Rashid plans to merge Kwong Yik with DCB Bank.
Rashid Hussain said it will not be consolidating the results of Kwong Yik until the transfer of the investment to DCB Holdings is completed.
